daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: the noun of yakun; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾: conjoined to أهل; ﴿مُنْفَكِّينَ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of yakun; ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and of the genitive; ﴿تَأْتِيَهُمُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after ḥattā, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْبَيِّنَةُ﴾: agent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to منفكين.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾: badal (substitute) for البينة; ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) رسول; ﴿يَتْلُوا﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿صُحُفاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مُطَهَّرَةً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is an adjective of رسول.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿فِيها﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are the fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿كُتُبٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿قَيِّمَةٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is an adjective of صحفا.

daas-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.
﴿أُوتُوا﴾: a passive past verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تفرق; ﴿ما جاءَتْهُمُ﴾: ما is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and a past verb and its object; ﴿الْبَيِّنَةُ﴾: agent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿أُمِرُوا﴾: a passive past verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿لِيَعْبُدُوا﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason (taʿlīl), the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أمروا; ﴿اللَّهَ﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ﴾: ḥāl; ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached to what precedes them; ﴿الدِّينَ﴾: direct object of the active participle مخلصين; ﴿حُنَفاءَ﴾: a second ḥāl; ﴿وَيُقِيمُوا﴾: conjoined to يعبدوا, accusative like it; ﴿الصَّلاةَ﴾: direct object; ﴿وَيُؤْتُوا﴾: also conjoined to يعبدوا, accusative like it; ﴿الزَّكاةَ﴾: direct object. ﴿وَذلِكَ دِينُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْقَيِّمَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِي نارِ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause إن الذين… is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾: ḥāl; ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to what precedes them. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿هُمْ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ﴾: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, muḍāf to البرية; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾: conjoined to آمنوا; ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿هُمْ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, muḍāf to البرية; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الذين… is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿جَزاؤُهُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾: khabar (predicate), muḍāf to عدن; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is a naʿt (adjective); ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to خالدين; ﴿أَبَداً﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿رَضِيَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾: attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِمَنْ﴾: attached to an omitted khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position; ﴿خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من and has no grammatical position.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ﴾.
He means [by «البينة»] the Prophet ﷺ. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "لَمْ يَكُنِ الْمُشْرِكُون وأَهْلُ الْكِتابِ مُنْفَكِّين". The tafsīr has differed: it was said: they were not to be «منفكين», [i.e.] desisting, until [145/a] the clear proof came to them.
Meaning: the sending of Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an. Others said: they were not to abandon the description of Muhammad ﷺ in their Book — that he is a prophet — until he appeared; [then] they split up and differed. And that is confirmed by … [Translator's note: the sentence «ويصدّق ذلك» breaks off here in the source; presumably it continues with the next verse, ﴿وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾ (4).]

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَسُولٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
An indefinite noun made to follow anew upon «البينة», which is definite, just as He said: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ، فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ﴾. In the reading of Ubayy it is: "رَسُولاً مِنَ اللهِ", in the accusative, by being cut off (inqiṭāʿ) from «البيِّنة».

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ﴾.
«الانفكاك» may be in the sense of يُزال (ceasing, as in «ما زال», "not cease to"), and it may be in the sense of the separation you know. When it is in the sense of يَزال, it must have a verb [after it], and a negation must be with it; so you say: ما انفككت أذكرك (I have not ceased mentioning you), meaning: ما زلت أذكرك. When it is not in the sense of يزال, you say: قد انفككت منك (I have separated from you), and انفك الشىء من الشىء (the thing came apart from the thing); so it is without a negation and without a verb. Dhū al-Rumma said:
قلائص لا تنفك إِلاّ مُناخة * على الخسف أو ترمى بلداً قفرا
(Young she-camels that never cease except made to kneel in hardship, or [else] they make for a desolate land.)
He brought only (إِلاَّ) into it while intending by it the complete [verb] [Translator's note: i.e. «تنفك» in its full sense of separating, not the defective sense of «يزال»], contrary to يزال; because you do not say: ما زلت إلا قائماً (I did not cease except standing). [Translator's note: the verse is usually cited with «حراجيج ما تنفك» and «أو نرمي بها»; translated as printed.]

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَآ أُمِرُوۤاْ إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ﴾.
The Arabs often put the lām in the place of (أن) with [verbs of] commanding and willing. Among that is the word of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿يُرِيدُ اللهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُم﴾, and ﴿يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِئُوا﴾. And concerning commanding He said in more than one place of the Revelation: ﴿وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلاَّ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوا اللهَ مُخْلِصِينَ"; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ذلك الدين القيمة", while in our reading it is "وَذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ", and it is [145/b] among the things annexed to themselves because of the difference of their two wordings. It has been explained in more than one place.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ﴾.
«البرية» is without hamza, except that some of the people of the Hijaz pronounced it with hamza, as if they took it from the word of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: «برأكم» (He created you) and «برأ الخلق» (He created creation). Whoever does not give it a hamza may also take it from this meaning; then they agreed on dropping its hamza, just as they agreed on [dropping it in] يَرَى, تَرى and نرى. If it is taken from «البَرَى», it is without hamza; «البرى» is dust. I heard the Arabs say:
بفيه البرى، وحمّى خيبرى، وشرُّ ما يرى [فإنه خيسرى]
(Dust in his mouth, and the fever of Khaybar, and the worst of what may be seen — [for he is a loser].)

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qayyima
Medinan; and it was said: the correct view is that it is Meccan.
[Translator's note: the source names the sūra «سُورَةُ اَلْقَيِّمَةِ»; it is otherwise known as Sūrat al-Bayyina.]
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ والمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ البَيِّنَةُ﴾ ("those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not to be released until the clear proof came to them"): ”اَلْمُشْرِكِينَ“ is in the position of the genitive (fī mawḍiʿ jarr), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "the People of the Book". The meaning is: "those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and among the polytheists were not…".
And His saying: ﴿مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ البَيِّنَةُ﴾: that is, they were not to be released from their unbelief. The meaning of ”مُنْفَكِّينَ“ is "desisting from their unbelief".

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُو﴾ ("a messenger from Allah reciting"): it is nominative on two grounds. One of them is as a badal (substitute) for ”البَيِّنَةُ“; the meaning is: "until a messenger from Allah comes to them". The second ground is as an explanation of ”البَيِّنَةُ“, [i.e.] "the clear proof is a messenger from Allah reciting purified pages", that is, purified of defilements and falsehood. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 13] ﴿مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 14] ("in honoured pages, exalted and purified").

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿فِيها كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ﴾ ("in which are upright writings"): that is, writings without crookedness, straight, distinguishing truth from falsehood with evenness and proof.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿وَما تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ إلا مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْهُمُ البَيِّنَةُ﴾ ("and those who were given the Book did not divide except after the clear proof came to them"): that is, they did not divide in their religion [Translator's note: the source reads «مِلْكِهِمْ», "their dominion", evidently for «مِلَّتِهِمْ», "their religion"] and in their unbelief in the Prophet, peace be upon him, except after they had recognised clearly that he was the one they had been promised in the Torah and the Gospel. [Translator's note: the source also reads «وكَفْرِهِمْ»; read «وكُفْرِهِمْ».]

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿وَما أُمِرُوا إلا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ ("and they were commanded only to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion"): that is, to worship Him affirming His oneness, not worshipping any other along with Him. ﴿حُنَفاءَ﴾ ("upright"): upon the religion of Abraham and the religion of Muhammad, peace be upon him. ﴿وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ ويُؤْتُوا الزَّكاةَ﴾ ("and to establish prayer and give zakāt"): that is, to believe, along with affirming [Allah's] oneness, in the Prophet ﷺ and to establish his laws. ﴿وَذَلِكَ دِينُ القَيِّمَةِ﴾ ("and that is the religion of the upright"): that is, and that is the religion of the community (umma) that is upright in truth; so that is the religion of the straight creed (milla).

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هم شَرُّ البَرِيَّةِ﴾ ("those are the worst of creatures"): the reading is ”البَرِيَّةِ“ without the hamza. Nāfiʿ read ”اَلْبَرِيئَةِ“ with hamza, while the other readers are agreed on leaving out the hamza, just as they agreed in ”اَلنَّبِيُّ“. The original form is ”اَلْبَرِيئَةِ“, except that the hamza was lightened because of frequent use. They say: ”هَذا خَيْرُ البَرِيِّةِ“ ("this is the best of creatures"), ”شَرُّ البَرِيَّةِ“ ("the worst of creatures") and ”ما في البَرِيَّةِ مِثْلُهُ“ ("there is none like him among creatures"). Its derivation is from ”بَرَأ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ“ ("Allah created [baraʾa] creation"). Some said: it is possible that its derivation is from ”اَلْبَرى“, which is earth (dust). But if it were so, they would not have read ”اَلْبَرِيئَةِ“ with hamza. The usage is ”بَرَأ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ، يَبْرَؤُهُمْ“; no one has reported ”بَراهُمْ، يَبْرِيهِمْ“, such that its derivation could be from ”اَلبَرى“, which is earth.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾: that is, gardens of permanent residence.
